summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant rejection presented with dyspnea, cough, and nasal congestion over two days. He was treated by EMS with albuterol nebulizers for wheezing, which provided partial relief. Admission labs showed hyperkalemia with a potassium of 6.3 and a BNP of 27,000, though chest imaging revealed no acute cardiopulmonary process. He received kayexalate for potassium management and underwent hemodialysis the following day, removing 2.1 liters of fluid. His potassium improved to 5.4, and respiratory symptoms resolved with albuterol and Mucinex DM. Lisinopril was held initially but restarted before discharge. He was discharged home with an albuterol inhaler, Mucinex DM, adjusted sevelamer dosing, and home health follow-up.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
